title: One hand-written MCP-exclusion census, every other pin derived: stop re-breaking N test files per operator kind
description:
FOLLOW-UP filed by architect-c7fb990e on 2026-09-18, on governor-f32726f9's instruction (comment-1204078f on parent task-2c3f878b).

WHY. Adding one operator-only command kind (repository.publish_resolve, task-2c3f878b) moves hand-written whole-set lists and frozen counts in at least seven test files. Measured at HEAD 5d21c7c4:
- mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts :160, :230-251, :255, :280
- mcp-main.test.ts :220-246, :268, :270
- mcp-http/mcp-http-host.test.ts :694, :696, :725
- daemon-command-registry-human-approver.test.ts :387-421
- daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts :840
- daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts :318, :360-361, :413, :465
- daemon-command-registry.test.ts :431, :1131, :1221, :2103
Every kind-publishing row re-breaks them. The worker on task-2c3f878b found four of them only mid-step, which forced a block and a re-plan. The epic's own rail 3 exists because two rows bump the same literals.

WHAT TO KEEP. The hand-written list exists on purpose: it is the independent check that catches a production DERIVATION bug, for example OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS silently dropping a kind. Deriving every site from production would delete that check. So keep exactly ONE hand-written census of the MCP-excluded / operator-only kinds, asserted by BIDIRECTIONAL set-equality against the production derivation (global roster rail). Every other site reads that census, or production, instead of carrying its own copy and its own frozen count.

SCOPE. The pin sites listed above. Measure again at claim time: the set grows with every kind-publishing row, and some of these files may be mid-edit by that chain. dependsOn waits for task-2c3f878b and task-a47babf8, which edit several of these files.

OUT OF SCOPE: any production behaviour change, and the per-family arms (deployment.*, monitoring.*) that do not enumerate the whole set.
definitionOfDone: Exactly one hand-written list of the MCP-excluded kinds remains in the daemon tests, and it is asserted by set-equality in BOTH directions against the production derivation (MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS / OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS less session.open). Proven by a `git grep` census, quoted, that finds no second hand-written copy.

The other whole-set sites named in the description no longer carry a hand-typed copy of the list or a frozen whole-set count. Each derives from the census or from production. A drill that adds one fake operator kind in memory changes only the one census file's expectation, not N files.
The census still bites: removing one kind from the production derivation in memory makes the census arm RED, and that arm names the missing kind (quoted).
Gates quoted with their count lines: the full `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm typecheck`.

THE CENSUS HOME: apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts. The vocabulary module is 'the single place the human-only class is stated' (mcp-tool-allowlist.ts comment), so its test holds the ONE hand-written operator census.

Keep one non-vacuity guard, `expect(ROWS.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)`. A swept table must prove it swept something (global rail).

If it does not, assert the family maps' union equals the wired kinds with no overlap, which is partition-exact. Never write a count.
- Give the census arm a failure message that NAMES the diff. toEqual on sorted arrays already prints it; check that it does.
